page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by an Ampere Altra processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz, with 1 thread per core, and is configured with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the t2a-standard-2 delivers average single-core performance, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1812.29 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 24.01 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound workloads show limitations, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3594.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1997.0, both falling into the weak to poor categories. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 26.99 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 16.42 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

Given its dedicated ARM cores and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the t2a-standard-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for ARM64 development, testing, and lightweight web serving. It is suited for applications that benefit from predictable single-threaded CPU execution without requiring high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core parallel processing. Typical workloads include basic web servers, text processing, and software development tasks optimized for the ARM64 ecosystem.
